questions.stem: In surgical tracheostomy, which airway problem is an indication when a nasal or oral tracheal tube cannot bypass it?
questions.answer: Acute upper airway obstruction

questions.stem: Which indication for surgical tracheostomy applies to a patient who needs ongoing ventilation?
In which patients does surgical tracheostomy provide airway maintenance and lung protection?
questions.answer: Impaired pharyngeal or laryngeal reflexes, or major head and neck surgery (e.g. laryngectomy)

questions.stem: Which indication for surgical tracheostomy is about secretion control?
questions.answer: Long-term control of heavy bronchial secretions, especially with reduced consciousness

questions.stem: Why is surgical tracheostomy used when weaning a patient from ventilation?
questions.answer: Less sedation needed, and less anatomical dead space

questions.stem: How does surgical tracheostomy improve ventilatory mechanics?
questions.answer: Less dead space and airway resistance

questions.stem: Apart from ventilation, which two care tasks are easier with a surgical tracheostomy?
questions.answer: Suctioning and oral hygiene

questions.stem: How does surgical tracheostomy change sedation needs compared with a tracheal tube?
Which benefit of surgical tracheostomy concerns getting patients moving?
Compared with a tracheal tube, how does surgical tracheostomy affect the patient?
Which device lets a patient with a surgical tracheostomy speak?
questions.answer: Speaking valve

questions.stem: What is the mortality rate of surgical tracheostomy?
What overall complication rate is quoted for surgical tracheostomy?
In which patients is the complication rate of surgical tracheostomy higher?
questions.answer: ICU and emergency patients

questions.stem: Which serious hazard is a concern with oxygen during surgical tracheostomy in an intubated patient?
Which two ventilator settings are checked for fitness before surgical tracheostomy in an intubated patient?
questions.answer: Acceptable FiO2 and PEEP

questions.stem: Before induction in a non-intubated patient for surgical tracheostomy, what must be ready?
questions.answer: All equipment, including a cricothyroidotomy kit

questions.stem: How is an intubated patient positioned for surgical tracheostomy?
questions.answer: Supine, shoulder roll or head dropped, head ring, head up, neck extended

questions.stem: Which anaesthetic technique is used for an intubated patient undergoing surgical tracheostomy?
options: Spinal anaesthesia with a tracheal tube
Awake fibreoptic intubation with spontaneous breathing

questions.stem: How should drapes be placed during surgical tracheostomy?
questions.answer: So the airway stays accessible

questions.stem: What FiO2 is ideal during surgical tracheostomy in an intubated patient?
What main hazard goes with preoxygenating at FiO2 1.0 before surgical tracheostomy?
What happens when the surgeon is ready during surgical tracheostomy in an intubated patient?
questions.answer: Deflate the cuff and withdraw the ETT slowly until the cuff sits just below the cords

questions.stem: Besides withdrawing the ETT, what alternative is described for surgical tracheostomy?
questions.answer: Advance the ETT before the trachea is opened, then withdraw it

questions.stem: How is the tracheostomy connected to the breathing circuit?
questions.answer: Via a sterile catheter mount

questions.stem: What is the normal cuff pressure range for a leak check after surgical tracheostomy insertion?
What does needing more cuff pressure to stop a leak after tracheostomy suggest?
questions.answer: A malpositioned or herniated cuff

questions.stem: Why is FiO2 reduced again during surgical tracheostomy?
questions.answer: So the surgeon can achieve haemostasis

questions.stem: If there is a problem with tube position during surgical tracheostomy in an intubated patient, what is done?
questions.answer: Remove the tracheostomy tube and advance the ETT down the trachea

questions.stem: What does the surgeon do once tracheostomy position is confirmed?
questions.answer: Secures haemostasis and sutures the tube in place

questions.stem: Which drugs can be used for persistent coughing after surgical tracheostomy?
questions.answer: Morphine, benzodiazepines or low-dose propofol

questions.stem: In intubated surgical tracheostomy care, what should the inspired gases be?
For severe airway obstruction, what is the alternative to tracheostomy under local anaesthesia?
questions.answer: Awake fibreoptic intubation

questions.stem: For a patient with a previous tracheostomy, which preoperative investigations check for complications?
questions.answer: Preoperative CT or bronchoscopy

questions.stem: In a patient with a previous tracheostomy, what can stop the ETT passing even with a Grade 1 view?
What can old stoma tracts create in a patient with a previous tracheostomy?
questions.answer: Blind pockets causing ETT malposition or surgical emphysema

questions.stem: What may bleed at the old stoma in a patient with a previous tracheostomy?
questions.answer: Granulation tissue
